submission.hypothesis: The exact current owner cause of the locked Python graph expansion from 9 to 34 packages is the unconditional runtime dependency `mcp==2.0.0` declared in `pyproject.toml` (line 20) and the pinned `ordivon-protocol` Git dependency (line 21), which together pull the MCP SDK (and its transitive server/starlette/pydantic/uvicorn-style stack) and protocol dependencies into every Host install. The Host distribution carries MCP/server dependencies because both the MCP server console script (`ordivon-host-mcp = "ordivon_host.mcp_server:entrypoint"`, pyproject line 26) and the MCP client (`McpRuntimeClient` imported in `cli.py` line 26, `__init__.py` line 73/120) are compiled into the single `ordivon-host` wheel, so `src/ordivon_host/mcp_server.py` (lines 21-25: `from mcp.server import MCPServer`, `from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings`, `from mcp.types import ...`, plus starlette/pydantic) forces the full server dependency subtree into the locked graph even for CLI-only consumers. submission.causalMechanism: Direct causal chain: (1) `pyproject.toml` declares `mcp==2.0.0` and the pinned `ordivon-protocol` Git dependency in the flat non-optional `dependencies` list (lines 19-22). (2) Both the CLI and the MCP server share one wheel: `ordivon-host` and `ordivon-host-mcp` are both `[project.scripts]` entries (lines 24-26) over the same package, and `cli.py` imports `McpRuntimeClient` while `mcp_server.py` imports `mcp.server.MCPServer`, `mcp.server.transport_security.TransportSecuritySettings`, `mcp.types`, `pydantic`, and `starlette`. (3) Because the MCP SDK is a hard (non-optional) dependency of the package, `uv.lock` must freeze the SDK's whole transitive server stack (starlette, pydantic, etc.) plus `ordivon-protocol`'s subtree for every environment, not just for the server entrypoint. (4) This is the exact owner-level cause of the graph expansion from 9 to 34 packages. The expansion is NOT inherently an invalid split: the workload/policy explicitly warns not to assume a split is justified merely from dependency count, and docs (STATUS.md line 101) state "forced splitting is deferred while each still owns one coherent vertical lifecycle" and RELEASES.md makes `ordivon-protocol` a pinned cross-repo contract. The correct next falsifier therefore tests whether the server dependency subtree can be decoupled without violating identity/ownership, not whether a split is warranted by count alone.
